A similar view was taken in Kaushal Pati Pandey case where the court granted recovery rights to the Insurance company in case of no fitness certificate as on date of accident.

It was held that the obvious rational for a valid fitness certificate is the proof that the vehicle is working properly apropos all vital aspects i.e.
its break, indicator lights, wipers, seat-belts etc. are working optimally, so that the vehicle can be maneuvered on a public street without causing damage to anybody.
If there is default in any of these requisite conditions, then the vehicle itself would be a danger to public safety and would impose a traffic hazard.

To  have uniformity and consistency, Tribunals should  determine compensation in cases of death, by the  following well settled steps : -
 Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be  determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should
be made in regard to the amount which the deceased  would have spent on himself by way of personal and  living expenses.

Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of  active career

Having regard to several imponderables in  life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with  reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table  with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step 3 (Actual calculation)

The annual contribution to the family (multiplicand)
 when multiplied by such multiplier gives the `loss of  dependency' to the family.
